expectations.text: States that instructions to a model are not enforcement, regardless of wording or emphasis
expectations.evidence: CLAUDE.md is prose, and prose is rung zero — it's training, not enforcement, and training degrades under long contexts, compaction, and subagents that never even read the file.

expectations.text: Redirects away from rewording CLAUDE.md as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: There's no `.claude/settings.json` in this repo at all, so right now nothing actually *stops* either action — Claude just usually remembers not to.

expectations.text: Recommends permission deny rules in settings.json with concrete syntax
Recommends a PreToolUse hook for cases that need logic rather than a pattern match
expectations.evidence: neither of your two rules actually needs a `PreToolUse` hook; you got lucky in that both are expressible as static patterns... If you ever wanted `--force-with-lease` allowed but bare `--force` blocked... that's when you'd need a hook

expectations.text: Explains that the deny message should say what to do instead, not merely refuse
expectations.evidence: Consider adding a companion message so the agent doesn't just try `git push -f` as a workaround... If you need to fix a mistaken push, ask the user to do it, or use `--force-with-lease`

expectations.text: Recommends verifying the device actually fires rather than assuming it works
expectations.evidence: Verify it actually fires — don't skip this: run `git push --force` and an edit to a file under `src/generated/` and confirm both get denied... An unverified deny rule is worse than none

expectations.text: Recommends committing the rules so they apply to the whole team, not just one machine
expectations.evidence: `.claude/settings.json`, committed to the repo — not `settings.local.json`. A rule that only exists on your machine is the same failure mode as a CLAUDE.md line

expectations.text: Explains why repetition and capitals do not make an instruction reliable
expectations.evidence: States 'The ~1-in-10 failure rate isn't a wording problem' and mentions training degrades, but does not explicitly explain why caps/repetition specifically fail as a solution
